_dsl.trigger.designation: fires once per zone containing the position that carries a designation of this kind/annex which is IN EFFECT on the evaluation date
_dsl.trigger.designation_not_in_effect: fires for zones containing the position whose designation of this kind/annex exists but has no in-effect date yet
_dsl.trigger.no_designation: fires when NO zone containing the position has an in-effect designation of this kind/annex (i.e. 'outside special area')
_dsl.trigger.zone_ids: fires for the listed zone ids only
_dsl.applies_to.ship_type: list of: oil_tanker | cargo | passenger | other
_dsl.fact_level: REGULATORY FACT | INTERPRETATION | SOFTWARE RECOMMENDATION | REQUIRES VERIFICATION

rules.summary: Any discharge into the sea of oil or oily mixtures from the cargo area of an oil tanker is prohibited while in an Annex I Special Area (clean/segregated ballast and the reg. 4 exceptions excepted).
rules.fact_level: REGULATORY FACT (summarised from Annex I reg. 34.3 – verify wording against consolidated text)

rules.summary: Discharge of oily bilge water from machinery spaces in an Annex I Special Area is prohibited unless ALL conditions are met (ships ≥ 400 GT).
conditions: Ship is proceeding en route
Oily mixture is processed through oil filtering equipment meeting reg. 14.7 (15 ppm alarm and automatic stopping device)
Oil content of the effluent without dilution does not exceed 15 ppm
Oily mixture does not originate from cargo pump-room bilges (oil tankers)
Oily mixture is not mixed with oil cargo residues
rules.fact_level: REGULATORY FACT (summarised from Annex I reg. 15.3 – verify wording)

rules.summary: Outside Annex I Special Areas, machinery-space bilge discharge is permitted only when the ship is en route, the effluent passes through approved oil filtering equipment (reg. 14) and its oil content does not exceed 15 ppm; not from cargo pump-room bilges and not mixed with cargo residues (ships ≥ 400 GT).
conditions: En route
Approved oil filtering equipment (reg. 14)
≤ 15 ppm
Not cargo pump-room bilges / not mixed with cargo residues
rules.fact_level: REGULATORY FACT (summarised from Annex I reg. 15.2 – verify wording)

rules.summary: Outside Annex I Special Areas, discharge of oil/oily mixtures from the cargo area of an oil tanker is prohibited unless all reg. 34.1 conditions are met.
conditions: Tanker is more than 50 nautical miles from the nearest land
Tanker is proceeding en route
Instantaneous rate of discharge of oil does not exceed 30 litres per nautical mile
Total quantity discharged does not exceed 1/30,000 of the total quantity of the particular cargo (1/15,000 for tankers delivered on or before 31 Dec 1979)
Oil discharge monitoring and control system (ODME) and slop tank arrangements in operation (reg. 29 and 31)
rules.fact_level: REGULATORY FACT (summarised from Annex I reg. 34.1 – verify wording)

rules.regulation: MARPOL Annex I reg. 15.4 and reg. 34.4
rules.summary: In the Antarctic area any discharge into the sea of oil or oily mixtures from any ship is prohibited (the 15 ppm bilge exception does not apply).
rules.fact_level: REGULATORY FACT (summarised – verify wording)

rules.category: Heavy grade oil – carriage and use
rules.summary: Carriage in bulk as cargo, use as ballast, or carriage and use as fuel of heavy grade oil is prohibited in the Antarctic area (exceptions for vessels engaged in securing the safety of ships or in SAR).
rules.fact_level: REGULATORY FACT (summarised from Annex I reg. 43 – verify wording, including HGO definition thresholds)

rules.summary: In the Baltic Sea Special Area, discharge of sewage from passenger ships is prohibited unless the ship has an approved sewage treatment plant certified to the special-area standard (MEPC.227(64) section 4.2 – nitrogen and phosphorus removal) and the effluent produces no visible floating solids or discolouration.
conditions: Approved STP certified to MEPC.227(64) §4.2 special-area standard
No visible floating solids / discolouration of surrounding water
rules.fact_level: REGULATORY FACT (summarised from Annex IV reg. 11.3 – verify wording; phasing dates from Circ.778/Rev.4 footnote 3)

rules.summary: Discharge of sewage is prohibited except: (a) comminuted and disinfected sewage using an approved system at ≥ 3 nm from the nearest land, or untreated sewage at ≥ 12 nm, in both cases not instantaneously but at a moderate rate with the ship en route at ≥ 4 knots; or (b) effluent from an approved sewage treatment plant (reg. 9.1.1) with no visible floating solids or discolouration. (Passenger ships in the Baltic special area: see the Annex IV special-area rule.)
conditions: ≥ 3 nm (comminuted & disinfected) or ≥ 12 nm (untreated), en route ≥ 4 kn, moderate rate
or approved STP effluent
rules.fact_level: REGULATORY FACT (summarised from Annex IV reg. 11.1 – verify wording)

rules.summary: Discharge of all plastics (incl. synthetic ropes, fishing nets, plastic garbage bags, incinerator ashes from plastic products), cooking oil, floating dunnage/lining/packing materials, paper, rags, glass, metal, bottles, crockery and similar refuse is prohibited in all sea areas.
rules.fact_level: REGULATORY FACT (summarised from Annex V reg. 3 – verify wording)

rules.summary: Within an Annex V Special Area, discharge of all garbage is prohibited except: food wastes, cargo residues not harmful to the marine environment, and cleaning agents/additives in cargo-hold, deck and external-surface washwater – each subject to conditions.
conditions: Food wastes: as far as practicable from land but ≥ 12 nm from nearest land / nearest ice shelf; comminuted or ground to pass a 25 mm mesh; not contaminated by other garbage; ship en route

Cargo residues (not HME): ≥ 12 nm, ship en route, both departure and next destination ports within the special area, no adequate reception facilities available, washwater without cleaning agents harmful to the marine environment
Antarctic area: discharge of introduced avian products (incl. poultry) not permitted unless treated to be sterile
rules.fact_level: REGULATORY FACT (summarised from Annex V reg. 6 – verify wording, in particular the cargo-residue conditions)

rules.regulation: MARPOL Annex V reg. 8.2 / Circ.778/Rev.4 footnote 2
rules.category: Garbage – Special Area designated but not in effect
rules.summary: This area is designated as an Annex V Special Area but the special-area discharge requirements have not yet taken effect (reception-facility notifications outstanding). The general Annex V reg. 4 requirements apply. Company policy may nevertheless require special-area practice.
rules.fact_level: REGULATORY FACT (Circ.778/Rev.4 footnote 2)

rules.regulation: MARPOL Annex I reg. 38.6 / Circ.778/Rev.4 footnote 2
rules.category: Oil – Special Area designated but not in effect
rules.summary: This area is designated as an Annex I Special Area but the special-area requirements have not yet taken effect. General Annex I discharge provisions apply.
rules.fact_level: REGULATORY FACT (Circ.778/Rev.4 footnote 2)

rules.summary: Outside Special Areas, discharge of garbage is prohibited except food wastes, cargo residues not harmful to the marine environment, animal carcasses and cleaning agents/additives in washwater – each subject to distance and 'en route' conditions.
conditions: Food wastes: ≥ 12 nm from nearest land, en route (≥ 3 nm if comminuted/ground ≤ 25 mm)
Cargo residues (not HME) that cannot be recovered: ≥ 12 nm, en route
Animal carcasses: as far from land as possible, en route
Mixed garbage: the most stringent applicable condition applies
rules.fact_level: REGULATORY FACT (summarised from Annex V reg. 4 – verify wording)

rules.summary: Within a SOx Emission Control Area, the sulphur content of fuel oil used on board shall not exceed 0.10% m/m, unless an approved equivalent arrangement (e.g. exhaust gas cleaning system) is used under reg. 4. Written fuel change-over procedure and log entries (reg. 14.6) are required when entering/leaving the ECA.
conditions: Fuel ≤ 0.10% S m/m, or approved equivalent (reg. 4) – check coastal/port restrictions on open-loop scrubber discharge
Change-over log entries per reg. 14.6
rules.fact_level: REGULATORY FACT (summarised from Annex VI reg. 14.4 – verify wording)

rules.summary: Outside ECAs the sulphur content of fuel oil used on board shall not exceed 0.50% m/m (since 1 January 2020), unless an approved equivalent arrangement is used under reg. 4.
conditions: Fuel ≤ 0.50% S m/m, or approved equivalent (reg. 4)
rules.fact_level: REGULATORY FACT (summarised – verify wording)

rules.category: Air – NOx Tier III in NOx ECA
rules.summary: Marine diesel engines (> 130 kW) installed on ships constructed on or after the date applicable to this NOx ECA shall comply with Tier III limits when operating in the area (subject to the reg. 13.5 exceptions and Tier II/III switching procedures).
conditions: Tier III certified engines / operating mode switched to Tier III inside the area
Record the change-over in the engine log/ record book as required
rules.fact_level: REGULATORY FACT (summarised from Annex VI reg. 13.5; construction dates from Circ.778/Rev.4 footnotes 5 and 6 – verify)

rules.summary: Position is within a PSSA. Associated protective measures (areas to be avoided, routeing, reporting, pilotage, speed) apply – see the designating resolution.
rules.fact_level: REGULATORY FACT (Circ.778/Rev.4 Annex 2)

rules.regulation: BWM Convention reg. B-3 / D-2 (and B-4 exchange conditions)
rules.summary: Ballast water management to the D-2 performance standard applies to ships subject to the Convention (phase-in complete 8 Sept 2024). Where exchange (D-1) is used as a contingency or permitted, reg. B-4 requires it ≥ 200 nm from nearest land in ≥ 200 m depth (or ≥ 50 nm / 200 m where the former is not possible). Coastal-State supplementary rules (e.g. USCG, Australia) are not yet modelled.
rules.fact_level: REGULATORY FACT (summarised – BWM Convention text not in project sources; verify)

rules.regulation: AFS Convention Annex 1 (organotin; cybutryne per MEPC.331(76))
rules.summary: Organotin biocides are prohibited in anti-fouling systems. Controls on cybutryne were added by MEPC.331(76): from 1 January 2023 ships shall not apply or re-apply AFS containing cybutryne; existing cybutryne coatings are to be removed or sealed by the next scheduled renewal after that date (no later than 60 months after the last application). PSC may sample/inspect per MEPC.356(78)/357(78); survey and certification per MEPC.358(78).
conditions: Valid IAFS Certificate / Declaration on AFS
Cybutryne compliance evidenced (AFS Certificate / record)
rules.fact_level: REGULATORY FACT (cybutryne controls referenced in MEPC.356–358(78) in project; effective-date details from MEPC.331(76) – verify)

rules.regulation: Regulation (EU) 2023/957 amending Reg. (EU) 2015/757 (MRV) – maritime EU ETS
rules.summary: EU ETS and MRV obligations are determined by port calls (voyages to, from and between EEA ports and time at berth), ship type and size – not by the vessel's instantaneous position. Evaluation requires voyage/port-call data (Phase 2: Voyage Compliance module).
rules.fact_level: REGULATORY FACT (scope structure per Reg. (EU) 2023/957 in project) + SOFTWARE RECOMMENDATION (evaluate at voyage level)
